config.displays.cab_mode.description: Presents VPinFE for playing standing at a cabinet: larger text and targets, and no controls that need a mouse. It does not rotate anything.
config.displays.cab_mode.label: Cabinet Mode
config.dof.dof_config_tool_api_key.label: DOF Config Tool API Key
config.dof.enable_dof.label: Enable DOF
config.frontend.confirm.description: Ask before quitting VPinFE or powering off the machine. Closing the frontend never asks - the windows reopen from the Manager UI, so there is nothing to lose. Off is how VPinFE has always behaved, and the question is put to whichever surface asked.
config.frontend.confirm.label: Confirm Before Exit
config.frontend.hide_quit_button.label: Hide Quit from the Main Menu
config.frontend.paging_group.label: Page by
config.frontend.paging_size.label: Paging Size
config.frontend.restore_last_table.label: Restore Last Table
config.general.ask_where_new_games_go.de: On, an import that could go to more than one place asks which. Off, it goes to the one marked for new games without asking. Never asked where there is only one place it could go.
config.general.ask_where_new_games_go.la: Ask Where a New Game Goes
config.general.assets_dir.description: Root folder for assets shared across games rather than owned by one, such as manufacturer logos. Served at /assets/ and defaults to assets/ under the VPinFE config dir.
config.general.assets_dir.label: Shared Assets Directory
config.general.chrome_options.label: Additional Chrome Options
config.general.chrome_options_exclude.de: Which of the built-in options to leave off, one per line. For the case where one of them is the problem and turning all of them off would take the rest with it.
config.general.command_timeout.descripti: Seconds before a command is given up on. One that never finishes would mean no table launches again.
config.general.command_timeout.label: Give Each Command
config.general.game_root_dir.description: The folder holding your table folders, one folder per game.
config.general.game_root_dir.label: Tables Directory
config.general.hidden_asset_kinds.descri: Kinds of supporting file this library does not collect - an all-EM library has no ROMs. A table that will not launch still says so.
config.general.hidden_asset_kinds.label: Asset kinds to hide
config.general.hidden_media_kinds.descri: Kinds of artwork this library does not collect. VPinFE stops showing and counting them; the files stay where they are.
config.general.hidden_media_kinds.label: Media kinds to hide
config.general.language.description: What language VPinFE speaks. Auto follows the operating system. Table names and everything else your library holds are never translated.
config.general.language.label: Language
config.general.library_refresh_minutes.d: How often to re-read the library from disk, in minutes. It picks up everything, not just tables - media and assets added or removed beside them too. Zero never does, which is the default because a read walks every game folder: fine locally, real traffic on a network share. It can always be asked to read it now.
config.general.media_browse_dirs.descrip: Extra folders you can pick artwork from when adding media by hand. The game library is always available; anywhere else has to be listed here before VPinFE will read it.
config.general.media_browse_dirs.label: Browsable Media Folders
config.general.mute_audio.label: Mute Frontend Audio
config.general.on_table_exit.description: Run after every table. They run whenever the ones above ran, even if the table never started.
config.general.on_table_exit.label: When Any Table Exits
config.general.on_table_start.descriptio: Run before every table, whichever launcher plays it, and before that launcher's own commands.
config.general.on_table_start.label: When Any Table Starts
config.general.on_vpinfe_exit.descriptio: Run last. These run even if VPinFE is stopping because something went wrong.
config.general.on_vpinfe_exit.label: When VPinFE Exits
config.general.on_vpinfe_start.descripti: One command per line, run before anything else. Written the way a shell splits arguments, but nothing else a shell does - for a pipe, point at a script.
config.general.on_vpinfe_start.label: When VPinFE Starts
config.general.rar_tool_path.description: Path to unar or unrar. Blank auto-detects one on this machine.
config.general.rar_tool_path.label: RAR Tool Path
config.general.splashscreen.label: Enable Splash Screen
config.general.startup_collection.label: Default Startup Collection
config.general.table_start_required.desc: On, a command that fails before a table starts stops it launching - for something the table cannot do without, like a share to mount. Off, the failure is noted and the table starts anyway.
config.general.theme.label: Active Theme
config.install.display_name.description: What to call this device where one is listed. Defaults to this machine's hostname. Nothing is addressed by it, so renaming is safe.
config.install.display_name.label: Device Name
config.install.features.description: What this install is for: curating the game library (library), launching games on this machine (frontend), managing the other installs on your network (devices), and a rollup of all three (overview). Each one it has decides what the Console shows. Overview is the one that has to be asked for. Left empty the install is for nothing yet, and System is still there to configure it with.
config.install.features.label: Features
config.install.id.description: Written by VPinFE on first start, and not meant to be edited. Installs are told apart by this, so changing it makes this a different install.
config.libdmdutil.enabled.label: Enable libdmdutil
config.libdmdutil.pin2dmd_enabled.label: Enable PIN2DMD
config.logger.level.label: Log Verbosity
config.logger.terminal.label: Log to Terminal
config.media.asset_sources.description: Which online catalogs are searched for artwork. Empty means all of them. Names come from the sources list this install reports.
config.media.asset_sources.label: Online Artwork Sources
config.media.thumb_cache_max_mb.label: Thumbnail Cache Max (MB)
config.media.wheelset.description: Name of the wheel art set to use library-wide, a folder under a game's medias/wheels/. The reserved name logo shows each game's logo instead. Blank means plain wheels, and the active theme can override this with its own wheelSet option.
config.media.wheelset.label: Wheel Set
config.mobile.chunk_size.label: Mobile Chunk Size
config.mobile.device_ip.label: Mobile Device IP
config.mobile.device_port.label: Mobile Device Port
config.mobile.rename_mask_to_default_ini: Where a table has no configuration file of its own, send the masked one in its place under the name the table expects.
The word between the table name and .ini - cab sends tablename.cab.ini as tablename.ini.
config.network.http_bind.description: Which address to serve on. The default answers every interface, which is what it has always done - set 127.0.0.1 to reach it only from this machine.
config.network.http_bind.label: HTTP Address
config.network.http_port.description: Port this install answers on: the HTTP API, the Console, the Manager UI, and the remote and mobile pages. Named for the protocol rather than any one thing listening on it.
config.network.http_port.label: HTTP Port
config.network.library_url.description: Which install this one reads its library from, for example http://cabinet.local:8001. Empty - the default - means this install holds its own, which is every single-machine setup. Installs on your network are offered; type an address for one that is not.
config.network.library_url.label: Library
config.network.theme_assets_bind.descrip: Which address to serve theme packages and table media on. The default answers this machine only. An address rather than a switch, so a single interface can be named; 0.0.0.0 is every one. This port serves the table library, so opening it shares read access to it.
config.network.theme_assets_bind.label: Theme Server Address
config.network.theme_assets_port.label: Theme Server Port
config.network.verify_shared_library.des: On startup, check that the library this install reads really is the one on disk here, by comparing file hashes rather than paths. Reports what does not match and changes nothing else. Off by default, and ignored entirely without a Library set.
config.network.ws_port.description: Port the frontend windows and the theme talk to VPinFE over. Loopback only.
config.network.ws_port.label: WebSocket Bridge Port
config.themes.registries.description: Catalogs to offer themes from, most trusted first. The stock registry is an entry like any other, so a mirrored or offline install can replace or drop it.
config.themes.registries.label: Theme Registries
config.themes.repositories.description: Individual theme repos, each one a theme in its own right. Resolved before the registries, and named for the repo with any vpinfe-theme- prefix removed.
config.themes.repositories.label: Theme Repositories
config.vpinplay.api_endpoint.label: API Endpoint
config.vpinplay.initials.label: Initials
config.vpinplay.machine_id.label: Machine ID
config.vpinplay.sync_on_exit.label: Sync on Exit
config.vpinplay.user_id.label: User ID
config.vpsdb.refresh.description: How often to ask VPSdb whether it has changed.
config.vpsdb.refresh.label: Check for Catalog Updates
config.windows.backglass.screen_id.label: Backglass Monitor ID
config.windows.backglass.window_override: Position and size for this window, as x,y,width,height. Empty means no override.
How far to turn playfield artwork so it fills the screen. auto measures each image and turns only when it disagrees with the surface.
config.windows.playfield.orientation.des: How the playfield screen is physically mounted. Portrait means it is turned on its side in the cabinet. This does not rotate anything by itself - it tells themes what shape to lay out for.
config.windows.playfield.rotation.descri: How far VPinFE turns its own display so it faces the player. Leave at 0 if your operating system already rotates this screen.
config.windows.playfield.rotation.label: Rotate VPinFE Display
config.windows.playfield.screen_id.label: Playfield Monitor ID
config.windows.playfield.variant.descrip: Which playfield artwork this library holds: table.png, or fss.png for art captured in Visual Pinball's Full Single Screen mode.
config.windows.playfield.variant.label: Table Type
config.windows.scoreview.screen_id.label: DMD Monitor ID
config.windows.scoreview.window_override: Position and size for this window, as x,y,width,height. Empty means no override.
console.about.everything_a_bug_report: Everything a bug report asks for, in one block
console.about.press_the_usual_copy: Press the usual copy shortcut - it is already selected.
console.about.put_all_of_it_on_the: Put all of it on the clipboard
console.about.this_browser_will_not_let: This browser will not let a page write to the clipboard
console.app_settings.this_table_has_no_l: This table has no launcher to configure.
console.assets.correctly_named_files_tha: Correctly named files that nothing loads - a shared file every table has overridden, or a script named for the folder when VPX only ever looks for one named for the table. The second kind is usually a mistake worth fixing rather than deleting.
Every row, nothing hidden. The way out of any other view, and where you build a filter of your own worth saving.
Files left behind when a table was renamed, updated to a new version or deleted. VPX will never look for these names again, so this is the list that is safe to clear out.
console.assets.how_many_of_this_game_s.h:
How many of this game's tables actually load this file.

0 - nothing loads it.
Blank - there is no file to load.
console.assets.read_the_library_from_dis: Read the library from disk again and pick up anything added, changed or removed - tables, media and assets
console.assets.the_game_folder_this_file: The game folder this file belongs to.
console.assets.the_vps_file_somebody_sai:
The VPS file somebody said this is.

Blank - nobody has said.
console.assets.the_vpx_this_file_is_name:
The .vpx this file is named for.

Blank - named for the folder, so every table falls back to it.
The year the machine was released.
console.assets.what_a_table_could_use_an: What a table could use and has not got. Not all of it matters - a PUP pack is an enhancement, not a requirement - so read it as what is available to add rather than as a list of faults.
What the file is for - the backglass VPX loads, the table's own
settings, its script, and so on.
console.assets.where_the_file_sits.help: Where the file sits, relative to the game folder.
Where the files you rely on came from. Use it to bind them to their VPS records, so a later version of a table can be told from the one you have.
Who put the file here, as far as anything recorded it.

Unknown - nothing recorded it, which is true of most files.
Blank - there is no file.
Why this file is not the one being used. Blank while it is.

Missing - no file at all.
Orphan - named for a table this folder does not have. Safe to delete.
Unused - correctly named, but nothing resolves to it. Either every table has its own, or it is named for the folder and VPX only ever looks for one named for the table.
console.binding_editor.how_long_it_has_t: How long it has to be held before it counts
console.binding_editor.nothing_triggers_: Nothing triggers this - bind something to it
console.binding_editor.press_one_input_t: Press one input, two together, or hold to bind a hold
How many tables the collection hands out right now.
A dynamic one changes as the library does.
console.collections.how_the_collection_d:
How the collection decides what is in it.

Fixed - you put the tables in yourself, and they stay.
Dynamic - a rule chooses, so it keeps up with the library.
console.collections.name: Name
console.collections.the_most_tables_this:
The most tables this collection will hand out.
Blank means no cap - everything the rule matches.
console.collections.the_order_the_fronte: The order the frontend walks the collection in.
What you called the collection. It is what the frontend shows
when it offers this collection to pick from.
console.devices.a_vpinfe_install_answers:
A VPinFE install answers for itself. A VPX Mobile device runs
VPX and not VPinFE, so this install holds everything known about it.
console.devices.ask_every_device_whether: Ask every device whether it is there
console.devices.devices_that_could_not_b: Devices that could not be reached, oldest first - so the ones that have been gone longest, and are most likely worth forgetting, lead.
console.devices.every_device_this_instal: Every device this install has met. Sorted so that anything not answering is at the top, because that is what you opened this page to find out.
console.devices.every_row_and_every_colu: Every row and every column. The way out of any other view, and where you build a filter of your own worth saving.
console.devices.name: Name
console.devices.nothing_has_been_written: Nothing has been written to the log on this device.
console.devices.nothing_on_it_yet_send: Nothing on it yet. Send games from the Games list.
console.devices.this_device_offers_nothi: This device offers nothing to do.
console.devices.this_is_the_install_you: This is the install you are reading the Console from, so its entry is not something to forget.
console.devices.what_answered_a_vpinfe.h:
What answered. A VPinFE install reports its version; a phone
reports nothing beyond being there.
What is switched on and reachable right now.
console.devices.what_that_install_is_for:
What that install is for: curating the library, launching
games on that machine, or managing the others.
console.devices.what_this_device_calls.h:
What this device calls itself, or the address it answered from
where it has never reported a name.
console.devices.when_it_was_last_known_t:
When it was last known to be there - it announced, or this install
asked and got an answer. Not the same as when it last started.
console.devices.where_it_is_reached_read:
Where it is reached. Read off the socket it announced from,
never claimed in the announcement.
console.devices.whether_it_answered_when:
Whether it answered when this install last asked.

Answering - it is there.
Not answering - it was asked and gave nothing back.
Cannot be asked - it has never said which port it answers on,
which switching the machine on does not fix.
console.devices.whether_this_is_the.help: Whether this is the install you are reading the Console from.
console.games.author: Author
console.games.blank_where_this_game_is.h:
Blank where this game is matched to a catalog entry.
Unmatched means nothing can be looked up for it - no art,
no release list, no update. Open the game to match it.
console.games.deleted_the_table_runs_its: Deleted - the table runs its own script
console.games.extracted_this_table_now: Extracted - this table now runs the .vbs
console.games.how_many_vpx_files_this.he:
How many .vpx files this game folder holds.
More than one means several builds of the same machine, and
everything to the right is the folder's answer rather than
any one build's. The Tables page separates them.
console.games.name: Name
console.games.read_the_library_from_disk: Read the library from disk again and pick up anything added, changed or removed - tables, media and assets
console.games.select_a_single_game_to: Select a single game to launch
console.games.the_build_s_own_version_as:
The build's own version, as its author set it.
Blank where the file does not carry one.
console.games.the_machine_as_your.help:
The machine, as your library names it.
One row is one game folder, however many tables are in it.
The machine this build is of. Several rows share one when a
folder holds more than one .vpx.
console.games.the_pinmame_rom_this_build:
The PinMAME rom this build actually resolves to, aliases
followed. Blank on a table that drives no emulator - an
electro-mechanical machine needs none.
console.games.the_vpx_itself_the.help:
The .vpx itself. The identifier of record, and what tells
two builds of one machine apart - which is usually at the
end of the name, so this column is last and widest.
A row whose file is elsewhere shows where, and one with no
file at all shows the name its program knows it by.
console.games.the_year_the_machine_was.h: The year the machine was released.
Ticked where the frontend does not offer this build.
The file stays where it is - hiding never deletes anything,
and a patch base has to stay on disk.
console.games.ticked_where_the_library.h:
Ticked where the library describes this table but the file is
not on disk. A share that has not mounted looks like this, so
the entry is kept rather than removed.
console.games.what_kind_of_machine_it_is:
What kind of machine it is - solid state, electro-mechanical,
pure mechanical, or an original with no real counterpart.
What the machine is about - its subject, not how it looks here.
Comes from the catalog, and a machine can carry several.
console.games.which_build_the_frontend.h:
Which build the frontend offers when it can show only one.

Chosen - you picked it.
Automatic - nobody picked, so one was derived. It moves if
the folder changes.
Which launcher plays this file. A dot means this table names
it; without one the table follows whichever launcher is the
default, so changing the default moves it.
console.games.who_built_this_table.help:
Who built this table. Several names where it was a
collaboration.
console.games.your_rating_for_the.help:
Your rating for the machine, 0 to 5. Click a star to set it.
Separate from a table's rating, which is per build.
console.games.your_rating_for_this_build:
Your rating for this build, 0 to 5. Click a star to set it.
Separate from the machine's rating.
console.import_dialog.always_use_this_on: Always use this one, do not ask again
console.import_dialog.name_the_folder_fr: Name the folder from the upstream record
console.import_dialog.nothing_in_the_cat: Nothing in the catalog matches that name
console.import_dialog.nothing_was_select: Nothing was selected, so nothing was imported
console.import_dialog.the_files_keep_the: The files keep their names. Only the folder is named here.
console.import_dialog.the_folder_is_name: The folder is named from the record, so other tools reading this library recognize it.
console.input_watch.press_anything_to_se: Press anything to see what it is. These are the inputs on the machine you are using, and pressing one binds nothing.
console.launchers.a_one_way_copy_change_: A one-way copy. Change it on a machine afterwards and the two differ from then on - nothing keeps them in step.
console.launchers.also_copy_which_tables: Also copy which tables use it
console.launchers.it_arrives_with_the_sa: It arrives with the same name and the same id, so a table that names it there means this launcher. A program path that does not exist on that machine is reported by it, not here.
console.launchers.name: Name
console.launchers.no_launchers_yet_add_o: No launchers yet. Add one and point it at the program that plays your tables.
console.launchers.no_other_vpinfe_instal: No other VPinFE installs are known to this one.
console.launchers.ready_it_is_switched_o:
Ready - it is switched on and its program is there.
Cannot run - a path it names is not on this machine.
Switched off - configured, keeping its tables, not in use.
console.launchers.tables_that_name_no.he: Tables that name no launcher use this one.
console.launchers.the_program_behind_it_:
The program behind it. It only says something the name does not
where the two differ.
console.launchers.what_you_called_this_w: What you called this way of running a table.
console.locations.game_folders_here_whos:
Game folders here whose id a higher location already uses.
Blank is the ordinary answer. A number means the same game is
in your library twice - often the same tree reached two ways.
console.locations.game_folders_its_child:
Game folders - its children are games.
One game - the location is itself a single game folder.
console.locations.no_locations_yet_add_t: No locations yet. Add the folder your games are in.
console.locations.the_folder_this_locati:
The folder this location is.
The last two parts of the path, because a library is very often
called `tables` and two of those would read the same.
console.locations.the_whole_path_for_tel: The whole path, for telling two similar folders apart.
console.locations.what_the_disk_says_rig:
What the disk says right now.

Ready - reachable and can be written to.
Read-only - reachable, but nothing can be added.
Unreachable - not there. Usually a share that has not mounted.
console.locations.where_a_game_you_add_o:
Where a game you add or import is created.
One location holds this, and it is your choice.
console.locations.which_location_wins_wh:
Which location wins when two of them hold the same game.
1 is highest. Move a location up or down to change it.
console.logs.where_this_file_is_for: Where this file is, for reading the rest of it
console.media.art_left_behind_when_a.hel: Art left behind when a table was renamed, replaced by a new version or deleted. Nothing will ever look for these names again, so this is the list that is safe to clear out.
console.media.every_row_nothing_hidden.h: Every row, nothing hidden. The way out of any other view, and where you build a filter of your own worth saving.
console.media.files_nothing_loads.help: Files nothing loads because something more specific always wins - the catalog art still sitting under the art you made yourself. Worth clearing if you want the space, but each one is a fallback that comes back the moment the file covering it goes.
console.media.how_many_of_this_game_s.he:
How many of this game's tables actually load this file.

0 - nothing loads it.
Blank - there is no file to load.
console.media.read_the_library_from_disk: Read the library from disk again and pick up anything added, changed or removed - tables, media and assets
console.media.the_art_you_do_not_have.he: The art you do not have. Filter to one kind and you have the shopping list for it - select the rows and fetch them from the catalogs in one go.
The game folder this file belongs to.
console.media.the_vps_file_somebody_said:
The VPS file somebody said this art is for.

Blank - nobody has said, which is not the same as there being no match to make.
console.media.the_vpx_this_file_is_named:
The .vpx this file is named for.

Blank - named for the folder, so every table falls back to it.
console.media.the_year_the_machine_was.h: The year the machine was released.
console.media.those_all_have_a_file: Those all have a file. Select missing ones to fill.
console.media.what_the_cabinet_shows_for:
What the cabinet shows for this kind while there is no file of its own - a set, or another kind standing in.
That file belongs to the other kind, which is why this row still reads as missing.
console.media.where_the_file_sits.help:
Where the file sits, relative to the game folder.
Art placed since 2.x lives in medias/.
console.media.where_your_art_came_from.h: Where your art came from, with the unattributed first. Use it to see how much of the library you assembled yourself, and to bind files to their VPS records so updates can be tracked later.
Which of the twenty media kinds this row is about - the wheel,
the playfield, the backglass and so on.
console.media.who_put_the_file_here_as.h:
Who put the file here, as far as anything recorded it.

Unknown - nothing recorded it. True of anything placed before the ledger or by another tool, which is most files.
Blank - there is no file.
console.media.why_this_file_is_not_the.h:
Why this file is not the one being used. Blank while it is.

Missing - no file at all.
Orphan - named for a table this folder does not have, so nothing will ever look for it again. Safe to delete.
Unused - correctly named, but something more specific wins. It is the fallback, and it resolves again the moment the file covering it goes.
console.mediasource.choose_a_file_on_the: Choose a file on the computer you are looking at this from
console.mediasource.drop_a_file_here_or_: Drop a file here, or browse
console.mediasource.files_already_on_the: Files already on the machine VPinFE runs on
console.mediasource.no_folders_are_brows: No folders are browsable. The game library counts as one, and more can be listed under Browsable Media Folders in settings.
console.mediasource.no_game_by_that_name: No game by that name in VPSdb
console.mediasource.this_game_has_no_vps: This game has no VPS id, so there is nothing to look up. Search above to take art from a game that has one.
console.metrics.off_reading_them_runs: Off. Reading them runs nvtop, so it is asked for rather than assumed.
console.page.could_not_work_out_which: Could not work out which game that row is
console.page.drop_this_on_a_game_to_add: Drop this on a game to add it to that one, or drop a table to make a new game
console.page.give_the_workbench_the: Give the workbench the whole window
console.page.the_library_is_up_to_date: The library is up to date
console.remote.no_lists_of_your_own_yet_: No lists of your own yet - a filter collection follows a rule rather than holding what you put in it
console.remote.the_wheel_is_not_listenin: The wheel is not listening while a table is up
console.sections.an_extension_adds_a: An extension adds a feature to this install without being part of it.
console.send_to_device.no_devices_to_sen: No devices to send to. Add one under Devices first.
console.settings.each_check_runs_over_ev: Each check runs over every game. Turn one off here to silence it everywhere; dismiss it on a single game to silence it just there.
console.settings.these_run_as_whoever: These run as whoever VPinFE is running as, so anyone who can reach this page can run anything that account can.
